clue.text: Resent being urged to move on request

indicators.note: in a down-style charade 'on' places the shuffled word after the request word

parts.note: to beg is to request earnestly

indicators.note: letters made to move are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resents being pressed to move along when asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges URGED into RUDGE, and 'on' sets it after BEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge something is to feel envy or resentment about it.

clue.text: Old king with girl no risk of inbreeding here

parts.note: ex means former, old
Og was king of Bashan in the Bible
Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An ancient king marries a girl from outside, so no inbreeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Og, the giant king of Bashan defeated by Moses, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage outside one's own group or tribe avoids inbreeding.

clue.text: Knight in snub to monarch, brought up for punishment

definitions.note: plural answer for a mass-noun definition: acts of retaliation

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up reverses the letters, reading them upward
the knight's title goes in the word for snub

parts.note: a slap in the face is a snub
Sir is a knight's title
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A knight who snubs the monarch is hauled before her for punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses SLASIRPER: SIR in SLAP, then ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprisals are acts of retaliation inflicted as punishment.

clue.text: Poet with nothing to drink in his workroom?

parts.note: a dry place serves no alcohol
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: A poet sits parched in his study with nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dryden was the 17th-century English poet laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a major Restoration poet and dramatist.

clue.text: Platonic form? Not a Platonic relationship

definitions.meaning: one of Plato's timeless ideal shapes
a three-way love affair, anything but chaste

explanation.surface: A philosophy puzzle about Plato's forms and non-romantic love.
explanation.walkthrough: For Plato a perfect triangle exists eternally as a Form; a love triangle of three people is far from platonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's ideal geometric Forms are timeless; the phrase also means a romantic entanglement among three people.

clue.text: Watery grave I must escape

indicators.note: the letter named must get out of the word, so it is removed

parts.note: grave in the sense of solemn, weighty

explanation.surface: A doomed person beside a watery grave insists on getting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watery grave' reads as one phrase; it splits, with 'Watery' the definition and 'grave' giving SERIOUS, from which 'must escape' removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Serous fluid is thin and watery, like blood serum.

clue.text: Drain and cut up chips: Horace made them

parts.note: to sap is to drain of strength

indicators.note: the word chips is cut up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A cook drains and chops chips, while a Roman poet looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' rearranges CHIPS into PHICS. Horace wrote odes in the Sapphic metre named after the Greek poet Sappho.
explanation.definitionFit: Verses in the metre of Sappho, which the Roman poet used in his Odes.

clue.text: Gibbons became literally furious

definitions.meaning: the surname of the Tudor-Jacobean composer, whose first name is wanted
the hero of Ariosto's epic poem who runs mad, in literature

explanation.surface: Apes became furious, quite literally.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando Gibbons was an English composer; in Ariosto's poem Orlando Furioso the hero goes mad, so in literature he became furious.
explanation.definitionFit: First name of the Jacobean composer, and the hero of a famous Italian epic of madness.

clue.text: Drink the money got together for food

parts.note: soda is a fizzy drink
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Friends pooled cash for drinks and something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick bread leavened with bicarbonate rather than yeast, a staple foodstuff.

clue.text: Roman general's English base?

definitions.meaning: the triumvir Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus, rival of Julius Caesar
the nickname for Portsmouth, home of the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A question about where a famous Roman commander was stationed in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Pompey the Great was a Roman general; Pompey is also the nickname of Portsmouth, the English naval base on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Roman triumvir Gnaeus Pompeius; the other is the sailors' nickname for Portsmouth and its navy dockyard.

clue.text: A divorcee, Frenchwoman has paid to go without being thrown out

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: the paid letters go outside, on either side of the French word

parts.note: PD is the usual abbreviation for paid
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A divorced Frenchwoman pays up so as not to be evicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go without' puts PD around ELLE, after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To be expelled is to be ejected or forced to leave.

clue.text: Describing an Inquisition victim — an early Christian

definitions.meaning: an adjective formed from the name of the astronomer condemned by the Inquisition
followers of Jesus, who came from Galilee, were called this

explanation.surface: A note on someone persecuted by the Inquisition, an early follower of Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: Galileo was tried by the Inquisition, so the adjective from his name fits; a native of Galilee was a term for an early Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the astronomer tried in 1633; the noun means a follower of Jesus of Galilee.

clue.text: Goblin and Jack have a chat

parts.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous sprite
in cribbage 'his nob' is the jack of the turned-up suit

explanation.surface: A goblin and a man named Jack sit down for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially and chat with people.

clue.text: Secluded road needed for, say, extra practice

indicators.note: say signals that the next word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket
a way is a habitual practice or custom

explanation.surface: A quiet lane is needed for extra training sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter and keeper; it counts as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A byway is a minor road or lane off the main routes.

clue.text: On the surface, little outcome from this work of art

definitions.text: On the surface, little outcome from this work of art

parts.words: On the surface, little outcome from this work of art
parts.note: a carving that stands out only slightly from its flat background, low projection read as little relief

explanation.surface: A critic says a work of art achieved little.
explanation.walkthrough: The French bas means low; in sculpture, relief is how far figures stand out, here barely.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpture whose figures project only slightly from a flat background.

clue.text: The irresistible attraction of Calcutta?

parts.note: a cosmic object whose pull nothing escapes, sharing its name with the notorious 1756 prison cell in Calcutta

explanation.surface: Asks what makes the Indian city so irresistibly attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Hole of Calcutta was a cramped dungeon where British prisoners died in 1756; in astronomy a black hole has gravity no light escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Its gravity is so strong that nothing near it can escape, an irresistible attraction.

clue.text: Ace shot putter is superfluous

parts.note: a golf stroke straight from the tee into the cup, so the club for the green is never needed

explanation.surface: Reads like an athletics note that a champion shot-putter is redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the shot put; in golf an ace from the tee needs no putting, so the putter is unused.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf ace is a tee shot that drops straight into the cup.

clue.text: One who used to play in cement isn't moving

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints

indicators.note: moving letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A player is stuck fast in cement and can't move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges ISNT into NIST. 'used to play' hints that the instrument is old.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the plucked instrument of Renaissance music, now rarely heard.

clue.text: With which fairly posed geometry problems may 'be' tackled?

definitions.text: With which fairly posed geometry problems may 'be' tackled?

parts.words: With which fairly posed geometry problems may 'be' tackled
parts.note: a drawing instrument for geometry, whose name also reads as 'posed fairly'

explanation.surface: Asks what tool a student might use on well-set geometry questions.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument is a right-angled triangle for drawing; split, its name says a problem has been set squarely, that is fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: This triangular drafting tool is used to draw right angles in geometry.

clue.text: I will leave procession and rest in passage.

indicators.note: the named letter will leave the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: a train is a long line, a procession
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Someone drops out of a parade to rest in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will leave' drops I from TRAIN to leave TRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Sort of light fare-about a pound

indicators.note: the word for fare sits about, around, the pound letter

parts.note: fare is food, as in good plain fare
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A price list for lights, with some fare costing around a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A floodlight is a powerful lamp lighting a wide area.

clue.text: Waves or particles can be managed

indicators.note: the words broken into particles can be reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A physics debate on whether light behaves as waves or particles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particles can be' rearranges WAVES OR; physics' wave or particle puzzle is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee something is to supervise and manage it.

clue.text: Decorate old woman for contribution to first-aid

parts.note: to ice a cake is to decorate it
bag is a disparaging slang term for an old woman

explanation.surface: Someone decorates an elderly lady for her work in first aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold pack applied to a swelling or bruise in first-aid treatment.

clue.text: The game in Stravinsky's Jeux de Cartes?

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the French title

explanation.surface: Asks which card game features in a Stravinsky ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: The title Jeu de cartes means card game, so a card game feels natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecarte is a 19th-century French card game for two players.

clue.text: Chess, in a version mentioned by Virgil

indicators.note: a version of some letters is a rearranged form of them

explanation.surface: A Latin poet's account of an alternative form of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges CHESS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aeneid, Virgil's epic, this figure is the aged father of Aeneas.

clue.text: Sun's starting to go in — getting used to taking cover

indicators.note: the picked letter is to go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: inuring is accustoming oneself to hardship

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word Sun's is taken

explanation.surface: As the sun goes in, people get used to sheltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Insuring a house means taking out cover against risks.

clue.text: Read lines in live setting

indicators.note: the word for lines goes in the word for live

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
rows are lines, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud verses in a live performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look through casually, as when skimming a book.

clue.text: Some rhymes for "plutocrat"

parts.note: two short words that both rhyme with the quoted word and also, joined, name a wealthy person

explanation.surface: A poet hunts for words that rhyme with plutocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short words each rhyme with the end of plutocrat, and together they are slang for a rich, powerful person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a wealthy, well-paid magnate, which is what a plutocrat is.

clue.text: Fly-by-night lawyer displays low cunning

parts.note: a legal eagle is a sharp lawyer, so eagle alone stands for one

indicators.note: cunning means cleverly worked, so the word low is reworked

explanation.surface: A dishonest lawyer shows base craftiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly-by-night' looks like a description of the shady lawyer, but it is the definition: a bird that flies at night. 'cunning' rearranges LOW into OWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A large nocturnal bird of prey with ear tufts flies by night.
